method.heading: CMAP Method
method.summary: CMAP constructs an action tape by combining executed actions with future action positions. It first predicts a coarse future chunk and a per-step span-selection score, selects the maximizing contiguous window, and regenerates the selected span while retaining all coarse predictions outside it.

stages.title: Predict
stages.description: The current observation and visible executed-action history condition a coarse prediction of future actions and per-step span-selection scores.

stages.title: Select
stages.description: Contiguous future windows are ranked by their mean scores, and the highest-scoring window defines the selected span.

stages.title: Regenerate
stages.description: The local refiner regenerates only the selected span, merges it with preserved coarse actions, and executes the resulting action tape with receding-horizon control.

simulation.heading: Simulation Experiments
simulation.summary: We evaluate CMAP on eight RoboTwin tasks and three single-arm ManiSkill tasks, using 50 and 100 expert demonstrations per task, respectively. ACT, DP, and CMAP are each evaluated over 100 episodes per RoboTwin task.

tables.title: ManiSkill comparison

real_world.heading: Real-World Experiments
real_world.summary: We evaluate ACT, DP, and CMAP on the AGIBOT G1 and Leju Kuavo 4 Pro platforms. Together, these physical deployments expose the policies to contact dynamics, arm-hand coordination, sensing noise, control latency, and communication delay.

platforms.title: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation
platforms.description: The Kuavo setup controls one 7-DoF arm equipped with a dexterous hand from synchronized multi-view RGB observations at 10 Hz.

platforms.title: Contact-rich tabletop manipulation
platforms.description: The AGIBOT setup controls the right 7-DoF arm and scalar gripper from head- and right-wrist-camera RGB streams, with a 15-Hz policy loop and a 100-Hz low-level arm-control loop.

table.title: Real-world success counts and rates
table.note: Chess Grasp and Bottle Grasp are checkpoints within 10 shared Dual-Item Placement trials; Outcome Avg. aggregates five outcomes.

real_world.protocol: We collect 50 teleoperated demonstrations per task and use the same task-specific demonstration set to train ACT, DP, and CMAP. Each method is evaluated over 10 physical trials per task with matched observations and action spaces. Success outcomes are manually verified from recorded videos and logs.

ablations.heading: Ablations
ablations.summary: Matched configurations distinguish the contributions of executed-action history, contiguous masked regeneration, and score-guided span selection on the fixed RoboTwin diagnostic suite and ManiSkill.

success_failure.heading: Success and Failure Cases
success_failure.summary: AGIBOT G1 success-failure pairs isolate recurring contact errors. Successful examples establish centered contact and maintain object alignment through the decisive interaction; remaining failures concentrate around contact geometry, grasp closure, and object alignment.

cases.description: The gripper enters the cup opening without establishing stable rim contact, preventing clean separation.
Off-center contact redirects the applied force and fails to fully depress the button.
The chess-piece grasp misses a stable opposing contact.
The bottle is acquired at a tilted pose that can cause slip or collision before placement.

success_failure.extension: The current policy has no direct tactile or force measurements. The remaining failures motivate contact-sensitive span-selection scores and a recovery controller that can reopen a new interval when the expected contact event is absent.

title: CMAP: Continuous Masked Action-Tape Modeling for Visuomotor Manipulation
abstract: Action-chunking policies generate temporally coherent action sequences. We propose CMAP, a history-conditioned continuous masked action policy that extends this paradigm with selective local revision in continuous action space. CMAP treats each action chunk as an editable prediction: it predicts a coarse future chunk from the current observation and recent executed action commands, scores contiguous candidate intervals, and regenerates the selected interval while preserving the surrounding actions. CMAP achieves average success rates of 61.8% in the eight-task RoboTwin main comparison and 53.3% on ManiSkill. Real-world experiments further show consistent improvements over baseline methods on the AGIBOT G1 and Leju Kuavo 4 Pro humanoid platforms.
